Spain–United States Convention for the Avoidance of Double Taxation (1990)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley 10/2010, de 28 de abril, de prevención del blanqueo de capitales y de la financiación del terrorismo (as amended by Ley 2/2018 and Ley 11/2021); Real Decreto 304/2014, de 5 de mayo (Reglamento SEPBLAC); Real Decreto 1098/2017, de 24 de noviembre (Reglamento del Registro de Titularidades Reales); Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, de 2 de julio (Ley de Sociedades de Capital, Articles 9 and 14); EU Directive 2015/849 and EU Directive 2018/843 (transposed); EU AML Regulation 2024/1624 (application phase-in from 2027). UBO definition under Article 4 Ley 10/2010: direct or indirect ownership or control above 25%; where chain analysis cannot identify a natural person above the threshold, senior management is classified as the beneficial owner.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Hague Convention 1961; fallback: Consular Legalization)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate governing body or notary of the jurisdiction of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Hague Convention 1961; fallback: Consular Legalization)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, and attorneys-in-fact against: (i) EU asset-freeze measures, including EU Regulation 269/2014 (Russia/Ukraine), EU Regulation 2017/2063 (Venezuela), and EU Regulation 2017/1509 (DPRK); (ii) UN Security Council consolidated lists (Resolutions 1267 (1999), 1988 (2011), and 2231 (2015)); (iii) OFAC SDN List given the use of USD-corridor rails through Wise B2B and wire transfers; (iv) the Spanish national list maintained by SEPBLAC. Enhanced due diligence (EDD) is required for foreign politically exposed persons (PEPs) as defined in Article 1.2 Ley 10/2010, including verification of source of wealth and source of funds; ongoing transaction monitoring applies to the BPO payment rails, with wire-transfer equivalency checks per SEPBLAC guidance.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Mercantil Central (Central Commercial Registry) – www.rmc.es; online application for 'Certificación Negativa de Denominación Social' through the RMC Telematics Platform, also accessible via the CIRCE single electronic portal (www.circe.es)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Denominations must be expressed in Latin script; Spanish is the statutory default, with co-official languages (Catalan, Galician, Basque) admitted. Foreign words are permissible when written in Latin characters, are phonetically distinct from existing registered denominations, and are not misleading as to the corporate form. The by-laws must include 'Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada' or the abbreviation 'S.L.', although this entity-type suffix is not part of the reserved denomination. Identity and high phonetic similarity checks are performed under Article 407 of the Commercial Registry Regulation (Real Decreto 1784/1996).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The negative name certificate is valid for 90 days; extension is not granted, so a fresh application must be filed if the notarial deed is not executed within the term. Up to five alternative denominations may be submitted in a single request. Upon final rejection by the Registro Mercantil Central, the applicant may, within one month, file a recurso de alzada (administrative appeal) before the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública (DGSJFP) of the Ministry of Justice under Ley 39/2015, de 1 de octubre, with the DGSJFP resolution expected within three months; alternatively, the applicant may resubmit a new application with different denominations or, as a last resort, challenge the rejection through the contentious-administrative jurisdiction.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Acceptable for registration. Article 9 of the Ley de Sociedades de Capital requires the SL to have a registered office in Spain that is effective for legal and administrative service of process. For a remote BPO call center operating without a statutory license, a serviced or virtual office address with genuine mail handling and correspondence capacity satisfies this requirement. The address must correspond to the municipality of the chosen provincial registry, and the notarial deed must identify it. A bare mailbox without administrative substance risks recharacterization by the tax authorities under the 'effective place of management' doctrine, so the virtual office should be supported by a management-services agreement with the serviced-office provider.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low. Quantified risk below 5% in the first 24 months of operation. The Spanish Tax Agency (AEAT) conducts documentary audits rather than routine unannounced on-site inspections; SEPBLAC physical inspections apply to obliged entities under Ley 10/2010, which this non-licensed BPO is not. Unannounced inspections would be triggered only by anomalies such as irregular invoicing, unreasonable deduction patterns, cash usage (not planned, given Wise B2B and wire-only payment rails), or inconsistencies between the registered office and the place where books and records are actually kept.

Apostille processing for documents issued in non-Hague or partially non-Hague jurisdictions, including Spanish Ministry of Justice certification where required

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, de 2 de julio, por el que se aprueba el texto refundido de la Ley de Sociedades de Capital (LSC), together with the Reglamento del Registro Mercantil (Real Decreto 1784/1996). Key applicable provisions: Art. 4 (minimum share capital), Arts. 19-21 (public deed and registration), Arts. 22-31 (statutory content of the by-laws), Art. 62 (fully paid-up shares), Arts. 124 and 174-175 (appointment of administrators and adoption of first resolutions).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Provincial Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil) of the registered office, operating under the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública (Ministry of Justice); corporate name certificates are issued by the Registro Mercantil Central in Madrid.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura Pública de Constitución (notarial deed of incorporation) followed by inscription in the Registro Mercantil, publication in the BORME (Boletín Oficial del Registro Mercantil), and assignment of the definitive NIF by the Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: An SL must have share capital of at least €3,000, fully subscribed and fully paid up in cash or in kind before the deed is signed (Art. 62 LSC). The cash capital must be deposited in a Spanish credit institution and the deposit certificate (certificado bancario de desembolso) attached to the deed. A Sociedad Limitada de Formación Sucesiva with capital below €3,000 is permitted under Art. 4.2 LSC, subject to a 20% profit reserve, statutory restrictions on distributions, and limits on corporate debts. Notary and registry arancel fees are payable separately; the former state tax on Operaciones Societarias is not charged for incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The Founding Members of [●] S.L., acting as a universal meeting, unanimously resolve that: (1) the company is incorporated under the deed and by-laws, with an object covering multilingual inbound and outbound call center services; (2) the share capital of €3,000, divided into 3,000 participations of €1.00 each, is fully subscribed and paid in cash, evidenced by the blocking deposit certificate of [bank] attached; (3) the registered office is established at [address]; (4) [name] is appointed sole administrator, accepting office; (5) the administrator is empowered to apply for the definitive NIF and complete all commercial, tax and social security registrations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reservation of Corporate Name (Certificado de Denominación Social)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Central, Madrid (online portal: www.registradores.org)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the official application for a corporate name certificate, proposing at least three alternative names. The Registro Mercantil Central verifies that the proposed name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered company and issues a certificate valid for three months, during which the name must be used in the deed.
required_dossiers: Copy of NIE or passport of each founding member
Power of attorney if filed through a representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected as identical or misleading, the applicant may submit a revised form with new proposed names; alternatively, lodge a reconsideration request with the Registro Mercantil Central or apply for a different denomination.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of Corporate Bank Account and Blocking Deposit of Share Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish credit institution authorized by the Banco de España
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a bank account in the name of the proposed company ('[proposed name] S.L.' or the founder names), deposit the full minimum capital of €3,000 from the founders' own funds, and obtain a bank certificate (certificado bancario de desembolso) confirming the deposit and the blocking of the funds until the notarial deed is executed.
required_dossiers: Bank KYC and anti-money laundering declarations
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank raises AML/KYC queries, provide source-of-funds documentation; if the bank refuses the account, open it at another licensed credit institution and obtain a fresh deposit certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation of Articles of Association (Estatutos Sociales)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Incorporating shareholders assisted by a local abogado or the chosen Notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the statutory by-laws in accordance with Art. 22 LSC, covering: corporate name, object (multilingual inbound and outbound BPO call center services), registered office, share capital and participations, transfer restrictions under Art. 108 LSC, profit-sharing rules, administration and governance organs, and dissolution procedures. The draft should be reviewed by the Notary before execution.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Notary requests amendments to comply with mandatory law, revise and re-submit the draft; if disagreement arises, change notary within the same notarial district or seek a binding legal opinion.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Application for Provisional Tax Identification Number (NIF Provisional)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT), Delegación Provincial of the future registered office or online at sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File Form 036 (Censo de Empresarios) or Form 030, identifying the legal entity, the proposed registered office, and the applying founder. The AEAT assigns a provisional NIF with the prefix 'ESN' or a provisional code, which must be cited in the deed of incorporation and used for the bank account and subsequent filings.
required_dossiers: Founder's NIE or tax identification card
Proof of registered office address (lease or title)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is rejected or returned for correction, rectify the data in the electronic office or request an in-person appointment at the relevant AEAT Delegación; ensure the correct provincial delegation is selected based on the actual registered office.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of Deed of Incorporation before a Notary Public (Escritura de Constitución)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public with territorial jurisdiction over the registered office (Colegio de Notarios)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: All founding members or their legal representatives must appear before the chosen Notary. The Notary verifies identity and legal capacity, the bank deposit certificate, the name certificate, and the provisional NIF, reads the deed, and authenticates the signatures. The deed must include the by-laws as part of the instrument and state the exact amount, form, and payment status of the share capital.
required_dossiers: Power of attorney if a representative appears
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Notary identifies a legal defect (e.g., unpaid capital or an unlawful object), the parties must correct the defect and execute a new deed; any rectification deed must be signed before the same Notary and re-submitted for registry purposes.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Clearance of the First Deed Copy (Liquidación y Pago del IAJD/Operaciones Societarias)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Consejería de Hacienda of the Autonomous Community where the registered office is located
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 30 business days of execution, present the first copy of the notarial deed to the competent tax authority for settlement or exemption of the Impuesto sobre Transmisiones Patrimoniales y Actos Jurídicos Documentados (ITP-AJD). Obtain the stamped or formally exempted copy ('copia para la inscripción'), which the Mercantile Registry will require for registration.
required_dossiers: First authorized copy of the notarial deed
Modelo 600 or corresponding regional tax form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office assesses additional tax, pay the assessment with applicable surcharges or file an appeal before the regional tax court; if an exemption is claimed, provide the statutory basis and request an explicit exemption certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Inscription in the Provincial Commercial Registry (Inscripción en el Registro Mercantil)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Provincial of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the tax-cleared first copy of the deed, together with the provisional NIF and any ancillary documents, to the Provincial Registrar. The Registrar examines the legality of the deed and by-laws, and if satisfactory, inscribes the company in the commercial registry. The inscription is then published in the BORME.
required_dossiers: First copy of the deed with tax clearance
Completed registration application and payment of arancel
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a 'nota de defectos' or 'nota de suspensión', remedy the deficiencies within the stated period (usually 15 working days); if the registry refuses to register, file a 'recurso gubernativo' before the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública or bring a civil action.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtaining Definitive NIF and Registration as Employer with Social Security
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) and Tesorería General de la Seguridad Social (TGSS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Following the Mercantile Registry inscription, file Form 036 at the AEAT to convert the provisional NIF into the definitive NIF (starting with the country code and the CIF structure). In parallel, register the company as an employer with the TGSS using Forms TA.6 and TA.7 to obtain the employer account code (Código de Cuenta de Cotización) when the first employee is hired.
required_dossiers: Registry inscription certificate or certified copy of the registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the NIF conversion is delayed or rejected due to mismatched data, correct the data through the AEAT electronic office; if the employer registration is queried, provide the registration certificate and re-submit the forms electronically or at the corresponding TGSS provincial office.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: IAE Census Registration and Legalization of Corporate Books
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) and the Provincial Mercantile Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company in the Censo de Empresarios and declare commencement of activity under the corresponding IAE epigraph (call center and BPO services are typically exempt from IAE until turnover exceeds €1 million). Must also legalize the corporate books (Libro de Actas, Libro de Registro de Socios, Libro de Inventario y Cuentas Anuales) by presenting them to the Mercantile Registry for the corporate seal.
required_dossiers: Form 036 or 037 for IAE and census registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the IAE declaration contains errors, modify it using Form 036/040; if the book legalization is rejected, rectify the formal defects and re-present the books to the Mercantile Registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Work Center Opening Formalities and Occupational Risk Prevention
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: City Council of the municipality where the office is located and Inspección Provincial de Trabajo
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: For the physical BPO premises, submit a 'comunicación previa de apertura' or 'declaración responsable de actividad' to the competent municipal department, together with a fire safety certificate in accordance with CTE DB-SI (evacuation, detection, and extinguishing), structural load verification where applicable, and documentation of the occupational risk prevention plan (Ley 31/1995), including risk assessments and the designation of a preventive service. The work center is deemed cleared once the documentation has been accepted or no defects have been notified.
required_dossiers: Fire safety and structural load technical certificate
Occupational risk prevention plan and prevention service contract
Proof of registered office and layout plan
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipal authority requires corrective measures, implement them within 10 working days and provide photographic or technical proof of compliance; if the activity is considered a change of use without authorization, request an urban planning regularization or modify the premises to meet requirements.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No industrial installation license applies to a call center/BPO activity under Ley 21/1992 de Industria; reference classification is retained by the Ministerio de Industria, Comercio y Turismo. The activity is subject only to municipal opening control and workplace health and safety compliance.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Municipal 'Licencia de Actividad y Apertura' or 'Declaración Responsable de Apertura' for administrative office premises; no separate industrial or manufacturing permit is required.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio para la Transición Ecológica y el Reto Demográfico (MITERD) as national reference; municipal environmental technical unit for urban office activities
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from full EIA. A call center and BPO office activity is not listed in Annexes I or II of Ley 21/2013 de Evaluación Ambiental. Only a simple municipal environmental assessment, integrated in the opening licence or declaration, may be required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Zero industrial process discharge; domestic wastewater must comply with municipal sewer connection regulations. Waste (WEEE, batteries, printer cartridges) must be delivered to an authorized waste manager under Ley 7/2022 de residuos and RD 110/2015. The activity produces negligible VOC emissions; occupational exposure limits must comply with RD 374/2001 (chemical agents), RD 486/1997 (workplace conditions), and RD 664/1997 (biological agents).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification in accordance with CTE DB-SI (fire resistance, evacuation, detection, and suppression) submitted with the municipal opening licence; structural load inspection by a qualified technician where the building configuration requires it; and work center occupational clearance following compliance with Ley 31/1995 de Prevención de Riesgos Laborales, including risk assessment, designation of a preventive service, and medical surveillance arrangements.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) - Spanish Tax Agency, official portal https://www.agenciatributaria.es/
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Spanish SL entities obtain NIF (TIN equivalent) automatically upon incorporation via notary public and Mercantile Registry filing. Foreign-owned SLs follow identical process; non-resident shareholders must appoint a tax representative for AEAT registration and ongoing compliance.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box elections; Spanish SLs are subject to mandatory entity-level taxation under Impuesto sobre Sociedades. Limited statutory regimes available for holding companies or hybrid mismatches, but no broad elective treatment for non-residents.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory real-time facturación electrónica for all taxable supplies; full API integration with AEAT required for issuance of digital stamps, invoice validation, and clearance compliance.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% VAT applies to exports of goods outside the EU or offshore services supplied to non-EU clients, provided strict documentary proof of export and non-resident recipient status.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration, Bill of Lading, Inward Remittance Certificate
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: AEAT may conduct retrospective audits resulting in penalties up to 100% of evaded tax plus interest and surcharges; fraudulent zero-rating claims trigger criminal prosecution and full clawback of benefits.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España, operating within the Eurosystem under the monetary authority of the European Central Bank; foreign-exchange and payment-services rules are principally derived from European Union law, Spanish banking law, anti-money-laundering legislation, and Banco de España supervisory requirements.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Spain uses the euro, which is fully convertible for ordinary current-account and capital-account transactions. Spain has no general exchange-control regime, no general requirement to obtain prior approval for foreign investment funding, and no general restriction on repatriation of dividends, interest, service fees, liquidation proceeds, or intercompany balances. Payments remain subject to bank AML, sanctions, beneficial-ownership, tax-residency, transfer-pricing, and source-of-funds controls. Dividend distributions require distributable profits, satisfaction of Spanish corporate-law reserve requirements, approval of annual accounts and the distribution, and applicable withholding-tax analysis. Outbound payments to related parties or low-tax jurisdictions may receive enhanced scrutiny and must be supported by contracts, evidence of services, arm's-length pricing, and tax documentation. Cross-border payments may also trigger statistical reporting, foreign-investment reporting, or information requests depending on transaction type, counterparty, amount, and reporting thresholds.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Spain has no statutory general obligation requiring a Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada to repatriate export proceeds to Spain, surrender foreign-currency receipts, convert receipts into euros, or convert a prescribed percentage within a fixed period. The company may retain foreign-currency balances with an authorized institution, subject to its bank's account terms and applicable reporting obligations. For a BPO and call-center business, receipts are generally service-export receipts rather than merchandise-export proceeds. The company should maintain invoices, contracts, service-delivery evidence, VAT treatment, customer due-diligence records, bank advices, and reconciliation between invoicing, collections, and accounting. Any applicable Banco de España external-sector or foreign-investment reporting must be assessed by transaction type and threshold; such reporting is not a currency-surrender requirement.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium to High for supplementary collections, payments, and foreign-currency treasury; Low to Medium as the sole banking relationship. Wise Europe SA and comparable providers may offer business payment services to eligible Spanish companies, but availability depends on product scope, residence, industry, transaction profile, currencies, and risk approval. An electronic-money institution is not generally a deposit-taking bank, and safeguarded customer funds do not provide the same deposit-protection or credit facilities as bank deposits. The company should retain a Spanish or other EEA bank as its primary account for share-capital evidence, payroll, taxes, regulated counterparties, liquidity reserves, and contingency access. EMI accounts may be restricted for client-money flows, nested payment activity, high-volume consumer payments, cash-like transactions, sanctioned geographies, virtual-asset activity, or unexplained third-party receipts. Use of Wise B2B or another EMI must comply with its user agreement, PSD2-related requirements, Spanish AML rules, sanctions controls, and complete source-of-funds documentation.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Spanish law does not impose a universal requirement that all directors physically attend a branch to open a corporate account. Remote onboarding may be permitted using qualified or reliable electronic identification, video identification, corporate-registry verification, and bank-specific procedures. Banks may nevertheless require a branch appointment, live video interview, notarized or apostilled documents, certified translations, an in-person signature, or physical appearance of directors, authorized signatories, ultimate beneficial owners, or foreign shareholders. A Spanish registered office, Spanish tax identification number, valid company registration, and an operational nexus substantially improve remote-onboarding viability. The bank may refuse remote onboarding where ownership is layered, documents are foreign, the business model is considered payment-intermediary-like, expected flows are inconsistent with the stated activity, or enhanced due diligence cannot be completed.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign shareholder or director with incomplete identification, expired passport, inconsistent spelling, or undocumented tax residence.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current passport or national identity document; proof of residential address; foreign tax-identification evidence; certified Spanish or English translation where requested; notarized, apostilled, or legalized documents where required; completed tax-residency self-certification; and a signed ownership and control chart.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear ultimate beneficial ownership or nominee, trust, holding-company, or multi-layer corporate ownership.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Group structure chart to natural-person ultimate owners; certificates of incorporation and good standing for each relevant entity; shareholder registers; constitutional documents; director registers; trust or foundation instruments where applicable; beneficial-owner declarations; corporate resolutions; and evidence of control rights.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: New SL with no operating history and projected cross-border receipts that appear disproportionate to paid-in capital.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed business plan; signed or draft customer contracts; pricing schedule; sales pipeline; staffing plan; expected monthly transaction matrix by country, currency, payer, and purpose; 12-month cash-flow forecast; source-of-funds evidence for shareholders; and explanation of why operating receipts exceed initial capital.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: BPO activity involving high-volume outbound tele-sales, consumer data, commission flows, or payments received for third parties.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Service agreements; evidence that the company is a service provider rather than a payment intermediary; customer and payer-flow diagram; prohibition of unauthorized client-money commingling; data-protection and call-compliance policies; sample invoices; merchant or platform agreements; and written confirmation of who bears refund, chargeback, and consumer-law obligations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payments involving Latin America, high-risk jurisdictions, sanctioned countries, politically exposed persons, or counterparties with opaque ownership.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Country-risk policy; sanctions-screening procedure; payer and beneficiary identification; beneficial-owner checks; adverse-media results; transaction rationale; contracts and invoices; proof of services; escalation records; and documented refusal procedures for prohibited or unexplained transactions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Frequent inbound payments from unrelated third parties or receipts that do not match customer invoices.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Aged accounts-receivable ledger; invoice-to-bank reconciliation; customer master file; contractual assignment or agency documentation; payment remittance information; explanation of marketplace or group-company settlement arrangements; and controls preventing pass-through payment activity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of personal accounts, virtual offices, unverified remote workers, or an address inconsistent with the declared business.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Commercial lease or registered-office evidence; utility or occupancy documentation; payroll or contractor records; employment and outsourcing agreements; operational workflow; technology and telephony records; and a written segregation policy prohibiting personal-account use.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax-compliance or CRS/FATCA information mismatch, including missing Spanish tax identification number or inconsistent entity classification.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Spanish tax identification certificate; deed and commercial-registry extract; corporate-tax registration evidence; CRS self-certification; FATCA classification where relevant; VAT registration or non-registration explanation; accounting contact details; and confirmation of tax-residence country.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected use of cash, prepaid instruments, cryptocurrency, or unregulated payment providers.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Treasury policy showing bank-only settlement; documented prohibition of cash and crypto exposure unless separately approved; approved-provider list; transaction-monitoring controls; and independent evidence that all proposed payment providers are licensed or appropriately supervised.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route shareholder funding from an account held in the shareholder's legal name to the SL's account with an EEA bank using SEPA Credit Transfer for euro funding or SWIFT for non-SEPA currencies. Before remittance, complete the corporate resolution, subscription or loan agreement, source-of-funds file, beneficial-owner review, and accounting classification. Use an unambiguous payment narrative such as 'share capital contribution', 'shareholder loan', or 'capital increase funding', and do not describe debt as equity or equity as revenue. For a capital increase, coordinate the bank certificate or other evidence required by the Spanish notary and Commercial Registry, and retain proof of receipt and subsequent registration. For shareholder loans, retain executed loan terms, maturity, interest, repayment mechanics, transfer-pricing support, and withholding-tax analysis. The bank may request purpose information, LEI or corporate identifiers, payer ownership evidence, and supporting agreements. There is no general Spanish FX authorization or mandatory conversion into euros. Reconcile every transfer to the general ledger and report any applicable foreign-investment or external-sector information through the prescribed channel when the relevant threshold or transaction category is met.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For ordinary BPO service payments, use SEPA Credit Transfer or SEPA Instant where available for euro payments and SWIFT customer credit transfers for non-SEPA currencies. A SWIFT MT103 is the traditional customer-payment message; banks may now process the equivalent payment through ISO 20022 payment messages. Include complete ordering-customer, beneficiary, account, address, invoice, and purpose information. For supplier or cross-border service settlements, retain contract, invoice, proof of performance, VAT and withholding-tax analysis, and sanctions-screening evidence. Commercial letters of credit are generally unnecessary for ordinary BPO services but may be used for qualifying cross-border purchases or structured trade transactions through a bank, subject to documentary-compliance rules, UCP 600 where incorporated, sanctions review, and bank credit approval. For recurring payroll, tax, and supplier liquidity, use controlled payment batches with dual approval, beneficiary validation, positive pay or equivalent controls, and daily bank reconciliation. Avoid third-party settlement unless contractually documented and approved by the bank.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable EUR/USD and other currency forwards entered with an authorized bank or appropriately regulated investment firm, supported by documented underlying exposures, treasury limits, counterparty limits, confirmation procedures, and accounting treatment.

Non-deliverable forwards may be available for restricted or non-convertible currencies and are generally cash-settled in an agreed reference currency; availability is bank-dependent and subject to MiFID II conduct, appropriateness or professional-client classification, EMIR reporting and risk-mitigation requirements where applicable, sanctions controls, and documented commercial exposure.

Currency swaps and cross-currency interest-rate swaps may be used for funding or longer-term liquidity management with an authorized counterparty, subject to ISDA or equivalent documentation, collateral terms, valuation, close-out, EMIR requirements, board approval, and counterparty-credit limits.

FX spot transactions and scheduled conversions may be used for ordinary operating needs; treasury should avoid speculative positions, maintain an exposure register, and match hedge tenor, notional amount, and currency to forecast receipts or payments.

Options and collars may be available from regulated counterparties but require separate suitability, premium, valuation, accounting, and governance analysis; they should not be used without written treasury-policy authorization and clear evidence of the underlying exposure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 4 months after fiscal year end (e.g., 30 June for calendar-year entities)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines up to €3,000 per filing and potential administrative dissolution proceedings if not rectified within 12 months

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Modelo 347 Annual Declaration of Operations with Third Parties
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 31 January of the following tax year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines ranging from €100 to €1,000 per day of delay, with possible criminal liability in aggravated cases

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit required if the SL exceeds two of the following three criteria: net turnover of €8 million, total assets of €4 million, or average number of employees of 50
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Spanish General Accounting Plan (Plan General de Contabilidad)

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annual confirmation of UBO details and notification of any shareholding transfers to the Registro Mercantil within one month of change

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced 15% rate for newly created Spanish SLs engaged in an economic activity, applying to the first two tax periods with a positive taxable base (Art. 29.1 LIS). Prior-year tax losses may be carried forward indefinitely, but compensation is capped annually at 70% of the pre-offset tax base for net turnover below EUR 5,000,000, 60% for net turnover below EUR 20,000,000, and 50% for net turnover of EUR 20,000,000 or more; a EUR 1,000,000 minimum offset is always available. R&D and innovation tax credits, plus the capitalization reserve, may further reduce the effective rate.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_temporal_limit: Unlimited (indefinite carryforward with annual quantitative offset caps)

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 200 (Modelo 200) – Corporate Income Tax return; mandatory electronic filing via Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) e-Sede at https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es, using XML upload or the online form, authenticated by digital certificate or Cl@ve PIN.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (per tax period, ordinarily the calendar year; an SL may adopt a different fiscal year only with AEAT approval and pursuant to commercial law).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 6 months and 25 days after the end of the tax period; for a 31 December fiscal year-end, the due date is 25 July of the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: NIF (tax ID), registered legal name, NACE/ISIC code 7820, registered address and the residency country of any non-resident beneficial owners.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The SL remains the Spanish tax resident; non-resident shareholders must not be shown as issuer of the Spanish entity's invoices. Any foreign branch or permanent establishment derived from remote BPO activities must be separately reported to avoid PE exposure.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting profit or loss before income tax from the financial statements prepared under Spanish GAAP (PGC), reflecting all retiro BPO and call-centre service revenues and costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Intercompany transactions with offshore related call-centre entities must be recorded and eliminated or adjusted at arm's length; no margin of the Spanish SL may be shifted without a valid transfer-pricing study.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Schedule of permanent reconciliations (non-deductible penalties, representation expenses above statutory limits) and temporary differences (accelerated depreciation, provisions).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Management fees or royalties paid to foreign related companies must be supported by contracts, actual service evidence and arm's-length pricing; any expenditure lacking economic substance will be recharacterized and adjusted.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 4 (Compensación de bases imponibles negativas sobre ejercicios anteriores)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Application of accumulated tax-loss carryforwards to the current tax base, subject to the annual percentage caps described above.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign shareholders cannot transfer tax losses unless a formally approved Spanish merger or tax-group provision applies; documentation must trace each carryforward to the originating Spanish taxpayer.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 5 (Base imponible y tipo de gravamen)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable base after loss offset, to which the 25% standard rate (or 15% new-entity rate) is applied.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Since the SL is a resident entity, its worldwide income is taxed in Spain. No foreign income tax credit is available unless a double-tax treaty and advance submission of the relevant certificate is made.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 6 (Cuota íntegra, deducciones, retenciones, pagos fraccionados y autoliquidación)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross tax liability reduced by tax credits, double-taxation relief, withholdings and quarterly instalments, giving the final self-assessment amount payable or refundable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Withholding on the SL's future dividend distributions is separate and reported via Modelo 216/296; it must not be presented as a tax credit of the SL in Form 200.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing without prior AEAT request incurs a surcharge under Article 27 LGT of 5% plus 1% per full month of delay, capped at 20% of the self-assessed liability. If AEAT requires the filing, penalties escalate to 50%-150% under Article 191 LGT, plus late-payment interest. Zero-liability returns attract fixed penalties of EUR 100, or EUR 200 where gross receipts exceed EUR 5,000,000, with an additional EUR 5 per omitted data element. Failure to file quarterly instalments (Modelo 202) adds separate surcharges under Article 26 LGT.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 19% on dividends paid to non-resident shareholders without a permanent establishment; 24% applies to residents of non-EU/EEA or treaty-less jurisdictions. The rate is reduced to 0% for qualifying EU parent companies holding at least 5% of the Spanish SL for 12 months under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The non-resident beneficiary must be the beneficial owner and must provide a certificate of tax residence (TRC) in the form required by the applicable Double Taxation Agreement (DTA). The Spanish paying SL applies the reduced treaty rate at source upon receiving the TRC, retains it as supporting evidence, and reports the payments and withholding in Modelo 216 (quarterly) and Modelo 296 (annual summary). Where the TRC is produced after withholding, a refund may be claimed through Form 210 within the four-year statute of limitations.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory IRNR rates are 19% for royalties and interest paid to residents of EU/EEA states or states with a tax treaty, and 24% for residents of non-treaty jurisdictions. Treaty rates typically cap at 5%-10% for royalties and 0%-10% for interest, subject to beneficial ownership and the Principal Purpose Test under the MLI where incorporated into the relevant convention.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 45,000,000 net turnover threshold for full Master File and Local File documentation under Art. 13 RD 634/2015; smaller resident SLs must prepare simplified documentation when related-party transactions exceed EUR 100,000 per related counterparty or EUR 250,000 in aggregate during the tax period, and must still file Form 232 for related-party transactions.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Spain does not apply the offshore Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) found in common-law financial centres; however, AEAT invokes the abuse-of-law doctrine (Art. 15 LGT) and substance-over-form principles to disregard Spanish SLs lacking real premises, local management, employees and commercial decision-making power, especially where the remote BPO structure is purely a conduit. A Spanish SL carrying out call-centre functions must evidence local supervisory staff, telephony or IT contracts, client agreements executed in Spain and actual operational control to secure treaty eligibility and avoid permanent establishment attribution.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion – Corporate Income Tax Fraud (Art. 305 Código Penal)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately concealing inbound helpdesk or outbound tele-sales revenue from Spanish clients using dual accounting, under-invoicing, or channelling payments through opaque offshore related entities.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Imprisonment of 2 to 6 years, fines of 2-6 times the defrauded tax, loss of subsidies and public procurement rights, and administrative penalties of 50% to 150% of the tax deficiency under Article 191 LGT.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are jointly and severally liable for the defrauded corporate tax debt. In criminal tax fraud they face travel bans, disqualification from acting as administrators for up to 10 years, personal asset attachment and imprisonment where a shell structure was used to conceal ownership or revenues.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing and Documentation Breach (Art. 18 LIS, Art. 191 LGT)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a cross-border BPO structure with related parties at margins below arm's length, failing to prepare the Local File, omitting Form 232 related-party reporting, or charging service fees for functions genuinely performed in Spain.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: AEAT may assess additional taxable income; incomplete transfer-pricing documentation triggers a penalty of 15% of the value of the related-party operations, while the total absence of documentation leads to a 50% penalty on the tax-base adjustment, plus late-payment interest and surcharges.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign fictitious intercompany agreements or authorize non-compliant transfer-pricing policies may be held personally liable for the unpaid tax debt. Deliberate manipulation of intercompany margins can also ground criminal prosecution, travel restrictions and disqualification orders.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Employment and Social Security Evasion (Art. 307 Código Penal)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Misclassifying call-centre agents as independent contractors despite employment subordination, or under-declaring employer social security contributions for a BPO workforce located and controlled in Spain.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recovery of unpaid social security contributions plus surcharges of at least 20%, administrative sanctions up to EUR 187,515 for very serious violations; criminal liability with imprisonment of 3 to 6 months and fines if the defrauded social security amount exceeds EUR 50,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are criminally responsible for unpaid social security amounts and may face corporate veil piercing, forced contribution from personal assets, travel bans and disqualification from public benefits. Persistent unlawful conduct can trigger a judicial prohibition from managing companies for several years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Economic Substance Failure / AML Deficiency
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Establishing an SL in Spain without a physical office, local workforce or genuine management activity while channelling client funds through the Spanish legal entity to a foreign related call centre; failing to perform AML/KYC checks on Wise B2B and wire-transfer payment rails.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The SL may be taxed as a disregarded entity with attribution of Spanish-source income to the foreign principal, and the foreign shareholder may become exposed to a Spanish permanent establishment. Violations of AML Law 10/2010 carry fines up to EUR 5,000,000; financial authorities may freeze accounts, issue cease-and-desist orders and revoke payment-rail access.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face judicial lifting of the corporate veil, effectively removing limited liability, with attachment of personal assets, travel bans, and potential imprisonment for money laundering if funds are knowingly routed through a purely artificial Spanish entity.
